newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar-linked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar-linked bonds close higher.

text.p: Israeli dollar-linked bonds closed sharply higher on Tuesday following the cabinet's approval of a second round of budget cuts, traders said.
On Monday the cabinet voted in favour of another 1.2 billion shekels in spending cuts for 1997 and 600 million shekels in new income.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: -0.03 to 170.66
* CPI-linked government bonds: -0.06 to 171.38
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.23 pct to 169.43
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.01 pct to 172.25
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 162.16
Volume was moderate at 148 million shekels with relatively low volume of only 41 million shekels in the Makams.
"CPI-linked bonds closed slightly lower today because of a moderate decline in medium-term bonds. Long bonds rose and short bonds closed unchanged," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"Yields on the inflation linked bonds fell during the last month from 5.5 percent to 4.55 percent. The market has now reached an equilibrium," said Gidi Halpern, investments manager at Meitav Securities and Investments.
"The rise in unlinked bonds was very moderate. These bonds reflect expectations for 1997 inflation of 9 to 9.25 percent against expectations of 13 percent three months ago," Halpern said.
Traders noted that the Makams were also mixed after yields fell to 14.25 percent, which is considered to be very low.
The main gainers were dollar-linked bonds as the market expects the Bank of Israel to lower interest rates after parliament approves the 1997 budget. The deadline is December 31.

"Approval of the budget (by parliament) will lead to a reduction of interest rates and a devaluation of the shekel. The central bank might lower its base rate for December by 0.5 percentage point. After the approval of the budget the central bank will cut the rate by another 1.5 to 2.0 percent," Halpern said.
The current base rate is 15.2 percent.
The Leumi trader said there were almost no sellers of dollar-linked bonds.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.28 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
